subject: Copywriting
title: Helen Lansdowne Resor: The First Woman
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Helen Lansdowne Resor: The First Woman.

hook.text: In 1911, Helen Lansdowne wrote 'A skin you love to touch' for Woodbury's Soap. It was the first sex appeal ad.

buildup.text: She joined J. Walter Thompson and became the highest-paid woman in advertising. Her copy spoke to women as people.

discovery.text: Lansdowne pioneered testimonial advertising, getting socialites and celebrities to endorse products authentically.

twist.text: Despite her dominance, history mostly forgot her while male contemporaries became legends. She was erased for decades.

climax.text: She ran JWT's creative department for 30 years. The agency became the world's largest under her creative direction.

punchline.text: She invented sex appeal in ads. History forgot to credit her.

quiz.question: What copywriting technique did Helen Lansdowne pioneer?

details.summary: Helen Lansdowne Resor was the first woman to hold a major position in advertising, becoming a creative force at J. Walter Thompson in the early 1900s. She pioneered emotional appeals, sex appeal in ads, and testimonial advertising — techniques that still dominate the industry today.
details.whyItMatters: Resor proved that understanding the emotional lives of consumers was just as important as product features. She opened the door for women in advertising and transformed how brands spoke to female audiences.
takeaways: She was the first woman to hold a senior creative role at a major agency
Resor pioneered the use of testimonials from real people in advertising
Her emotional approach to copy revolutionized how brands spoke to women

faq.question: What advertising techniques did Helen Lansdowne Resor invent?
faq.answer: Resor pioneered celebrity and aspirational testimonials, emotional appeals targeting women's desires and insecurities, and the use of fine art in advertising. Her Woodbury's Soap campaign — 'A skin you love to touch' — was the first to use sex appeal in ads.

faq.question: Why is Resor less well-known than her male contemporaries?
faq.answer: Resor worked largely behind the scenes and was often credited as part of the J. Walter Thompson team rather than individually. Gender bias in historical accounts further obscured her contributions, though modern advertising historians have worked to restore her legacy.
